limitations: PROVISIONAL: PR #91 report v1 is an interim input, not the canonical PT-01 interface.
Evidence is a report fragment, not verified source context; symbol-only evidence can originate in comments or strings.
Lexical matches include declarations, same-name identifiers, macros and inactive code; they do not prove a call or platform dependency.
Raw evidence is withheld; locations, matched rule names and a SHA-256 digest identify the supplied evidence.
No conversion, execution, capability grant, compatibility certification or target acceptance is performed.
Representative coverage only; this is not a Linux support matrix and does not state that Linux applications run unchanged.

rules.reason: POSIX descriptor, file-control and directory headers indicate a POSIX-oriented API surface candidate; the header alone does not show which calls are used.
gaps: No POSIX compatibility layer is assumed; the public SDK does not provide POSIX headers or calls.
Select the concrete calls from source review; do not infer a Nagi API of the same name.

rules.reason: POSIX open-family calls return integer descriptors with flags, modes, umask and path semantics.
gaps: No general file-open API is exposed by this public SDK.
Review flags (O_*), modes, path encoding, symlink and permission semantics; do not substitute host file access.

rules.reason: POSIX read calls operate on integer descriptors and may return short counts, EOF or EINTR/EAGAIN.
gaps: No public general file-read API is available in this SDK.
Partial reads, EOF, blocking mode and error mapping need explicit adapter design.

rules.reason: POSIX write calls may write fewer bytes than requested and carry no durability guarantee by themselves.
gaps: The SDK does not expose a general file-write API.
Review short writes, atomicity, append semantics and cancellation separately.

rules.reason: Sync and truncate calls express durability or size-change intent over a descriptor.
gaps: No storage durability API is exposed by this public SDK.
Durability and size-change guarantees of any Nagi storage service are unreviewed; no equivalence is assumed.

rules.reason: A POSIX file descriptor is a process-local integer, not a Nagi capability, and cannot be transferred by numeric reinterpretation.
gaps: No generic descriptor API exists in the public SDK.
Descriptor duplication, inheritance and close-on-exec semantics have no reviewed mapping.

rules.reason: Path and directory calls assume a hierarchical filesystem namespace with POSIX metadata and permission bits.
gaps: No path or directory API exists in the public SDK.
Nagi file access is object/capability based; path-based namespace assumptions need redesign review, not host filesystem use.

rules.reason: fork/exec/wait style process control assumes POSIX process semantics.
gaps: The SDK exposes no process creation API.
Native process creation is spawn-oriented and fork() is not foundational (AGENTS.md); spawn authorization needs separate review.

rules.reason: pthread threads and synchronization objects are POSIX runtime dependencies.
gaps: The SDK exposes no thread API.
Thread creation and scheduling need a runtime adapter and authorization.

rules.reason: POSIX asynchronous signal handling and signal masks assume a POSIX process model.
gaps: No signal API exists in the public SDK.
Signal delivery and masking have no reviewed Nagi counterpart.

rules.reason: poll/select style readiness multiplexing is defined over file descriptors.
gaps: No readiness API exists in the public SDK.
Readiness semantics over Nagi handles are not specified here.

rules.reason: BSD/POSIX socket calls and headers assume descriptor-based networking.
gaps: No public SDK socket API exists.
Networking belongs to a Nagi user-space service; do not use host sockets as a substitute.

rules.reason: Memory mapping and POSIX shared memory assume descriptor-backed mappings and protection flags.
gaps: No mapping API exists in the public SDK.
Memory authority is a kernel/capability concern; mapping semantics need explicit security review.

rules.reason: inotify is a Linux-specific file change notification interface based on descriptors and watch descriptors.
gaps: No file-change notification API exists in the public SDK.
Event coalescing, overflow, rename pairing and watch limits would need a Nagi service design; no equivalence is assumed.

rules.reason: epoll is a Linux-specific descriptor readiness interface with edge/level trigger modes.
gaps: No equivalent event-loop API exists in the public SDK.
Trigger-mode, fairness and descriptor lifetime semantics are unreviewed.

rules.reason: eventfd, timerfd and signalfd are Linux-specific descriptor-based event sources.
gaps: No equivalent API exists in the public SDK.
Timer, wakeup and signal semantics need separate design review.

rules.reason: ioctl/syscall/prctl and Linux UAPI headers depend on the Linux kernel ABI directly.
gaps: Adopting the Linux kernel does not by itself guarantee unchanged Linux application execution or Linux ABI exposure.
Each interface needs an explicit, reviewed userland design; no ABI claim is made.

rules.reason: GTK identifiers indicate a toolkit dependency and porting question.

alternatives.limits: Constructs logical presentation data; does not provide GTK widgets, event loops, rendering, IPC or rights.

gaps: Dependency classification only; toolkit structure and UI mapping belong to the UI analysis (NDP-06/PT-04).
No GTK runtime, widget set or event loop is supplied by the SDK.

rules.reason: GLib/GIO usage indicates a runtime library dependency (main loop, objects, file abstractions).
gaps: No GLib/GIO is supplied; each used facility needs a separate decision (replace, port or exclude).
GFile/GIO file access must not be mapped onto host files.

rules.reason: Qt identifiers indicate a toolkit dependency and porting question.

alternatives.limits: Constructs logical presentation data; does not provide Qt widgets, moc, event loops, rendering, IPC or rights.

gaps: Dependency classification only; toolkit structure and UI mapping belong to the UI analysis (NDP-06/PT-04).
No Qt runtime, moc, widget set or event loop is supplied by the SDK.
